overall: Okay, real talk. Call me out and Make it fun are the only two I'd put on camera. Callout has the most screenshot lines in the whole run: salad resentment, 'Checked their stories. Twice.', plane clapping, 'My feed is mostly food pics', 'Which compliment would you screenshot?'. Fun is right behind it and sometimes cleaner, because its jokes are softer and land on both poles ('a week in my cart', the vacuum person, 'my replies got slower and slower'). Watch callout though: plane clapping makes the ick sound petty, and 'not knowing anyone is the point' quietly changes what A means. Scenario is mostly fun's lines plus better prompts (roommates, brunch, late-night talks), which is honestly a great combo, but it cut the helpers from caregiving and dropped a word in second_chances. Quest and Kind are the same safe copy: Kind is so careful it's beige, and Quest's 'side quest', 'daily tasks' and 'level up' read like a brand deck pretending to be a gamer. I review games for a living; cozy players will clock that instantly. Oracle is last by a mile: 'the cards recall', 'your past card', 'the crystal ball replays' on every prompt is wallpaper, and cards next to money prompts looks like a slot machine ad, which is exactly the vibe a no-dark-pattern game should never give off. Cross-cutting issues nobody fixed: 'Their timeline isn't mine' is the Instagram-caption answer in every version, volunteering reads as the good-person pick in self_or_others except fun's, and where a writer gives only one pole a joke (fun on passcodes, success and marriage), that pole starts looking cool. If I were shipping: callout's lines where both poles get a detail, fun's where callout jabs one side, scenario's prompts. That's the version I'd screenshot for my audience and I'd say it's actually honest.
